Troezēn , ēnis, f., = Τροιζήν,
I.a very ancient city of Argolis, where Pittheus, the maternal grandfather of Theseus, reigned, near the mod. village of Damala, Mel. 2, 3, 8; Plin. 4, 5, 9, § 18; Cic. Off. 3, 11, 48; Ov. M. 6, 418: “prope Troezena,” id. ib. 15, 296 ; 15, 506; id. P. 4, 16, 15; Stat. Th. 4, 81.— Hence, Troezēnĭus , a, um, adj., of or
beionging to Trœzen: “ager,” Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 56 : “litus,” Mel. 2, 7, 10 : “vinum,” Plin. 14, 18, 22, § 116 : “carbunculi,” id. 37, 7, 25, § 97 : “heros,” i. e. Lelex, son of Pittheus, Ov. M. 8, 566 .—In plur. subst.: Troezēnĭi , ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Trœzen, Mel. 2, 3, 8.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
